item.title: Florida Leaders Ramp Up Push Against Tech Companies, Terrorism as Campaign Season Intensifies
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida government officials are stepping up efforts on two major fronts as the political season shifts into higher gear following the Labor Day holiday, according to reporting from North Escambia. State leaders have increased their focus on regulating technology companies and combating terrorism threats, with lawmakers signaling that artificial…
item.content:encoded:
Florida government officials are stepping up efforts on two major fronts as the political season shifts into higher gear following the Labor Day holiday, according to reporting from North Escambia.

State leaders have increased their focus on regulating technology companies and combating terrorism threats, with lawmakers signaling that artificial intelligence will be a central concern going forward. "AI is only going to get more advanced," one official noted, underscoring expectations that tech regulation will remain a priority issue heading into the fall.

The push comes as political campaigns across Florida have resumed after the summer pause, bringing renewed attention to policy positions and legislative priorities. The dual emphasis on tech oversight and security reflects broader national debates about innovation, regulation, and public safety that are playing out in state capitals across the country.

For North Florida residents, these state-level initiatives could have ripple effects on everything from cybersecurity protections to how emerging technologies are deployed in schools, workplaces, and government services.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos absorbed a lopsided 19-1 loss to the Biloxi Shuckers on Saturday night in one of their final regular-season games. According to the game report, Wahoos pitchers struggled significantly, issuing 12 walks while allowing 15 hits as Biloxi dominated the matchup.

The blowout appeared to serve as a low-leverage opportunity for several pitchers to get work in advance of the postseason. Ian Lewis Jr. was among the players who saw action in the game.

The loss sets up the Blue Wahoos' final games of the regular season as they prepare for playoff positioning. Despite the lopsided defeat, the team will look to regroup before the postseason stretch begins.

item.content:encoded:
A Cantonment man has been sentenced following an April 2026 incident that endangered a child, according to North Escambia reporting.

Colton David Gideons, 27, pleaded no contest to charges of child abuse without great bodily harm, simple assault with domestic violence enhancement, and reckless driving. Authorities say Gideons threatened a woman and forced her vehicle off the road while a child was inside the car.

The sentencing follows the incidents detailed in the initial investigation. Court records indicate Gideons' actions put the child at risk during the confrontation on the roadway.

item.title: Molino Woman Enters Pretrial Diversion in Amusement Park Burglary Case
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A 19-year-old Molino woman accused of burglarizing a local waterpark and amusement park where she once worked has agreed to a deferred prosecution arrangement, according to court records. Madison Lee Galle was charged in February with unarmed burglary of an unoccupied structure and criminal mischief, both felonies. The charges stemmed from…
item.content:encoded:
A 19-year-old Molino woman accused of burglarizing a local waterpark and amusement park where she once worked has agreed to a deferred prosecution arrangement, according to court records.

Madison Lee Galle was charged in February with unarmed burglary of an unoccupied structure and criminal mischief, both felonies. The charges stemmed from break-ins at facilities in the North Escambia area where Galle had previously been employed.

Under the pretrial diversion agreement, Galle can avoid prosecution if she meets the terms set by the court. If successfully completed, the charges would typically be dismissed and the arrest record may be eligible for expungement.

Pretrial diversion programs are commonly used in cases involving first-time offenders or situations where rehabilitation may be more appropriate than traditional prosecution.

item.content:encoded:

The incident occurred amid a gathering of more than 500 people, according to law enforcement. Details about the victim's condition and the circumstances leading to the shooting remain limited at this time.

The suspect is being held in connection with the incident as the investigation continues. Atmore police have not yet released additional details about the motive or the exact location of the shooting within the city.

item.content:encoded:
A brief window for rain wraps up this weekend as North Escambia prepares for a hot, dry stretch ahead. Sunday offers only a 30 percent chance of scattered showers and thunderstorms, mainly after 1 p.m., with highs near 91 degrees and mostly sunny skies otherwise, according to the National Weather Service forecast.

Starting Monday, the region shifts into a notably hotter and drier pattern. Afternoon temperatures are expected to climb around 90 degrees daily with little to no rain expected through at least the early part of the week. Residents should prepare for sustained heat and limited precipitation relief, making it a good time to ensure adequate hydration and account for increased cooling needs.

item.title: Escambia Schools May Close Buildings, Rezone as District Starts 'Right-Sizing' Review
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Public Schools District is launching a significant review of its infrastructure that could reshape how schools are assigned and potentially close underutilized facilities. The School Attendance Zone Advisory Committee will hold its first meeting this month to tackle what the district calls a "right-sizing" initiative. According…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Public Schools District is launching a significant review of its infrastructure that could reshape how schools are assigned and potentially close underutilized facilities. The School Attendance Zone Advisory Committee will hold its first meeting this month to tackle what the district calls a "right-sizing" initiative.

According to North Escambia, the committee will convene September 24 at the Vernon McDaniel Building on Pace Boulevard to begin examining school attendance zones and facility usage. The process could result in realigning attendance boundaries, rezoning existing schools, or permanently closing buildings that don't serve current enrollment needs.

The right-sizing effort reflects broader challenges facing school districts across Florida as enrollment patterns shift and aging facilities strain budgets. The committee's work will likely generate significant interest from families concerned about which schools might close or see boundary changes.

Parents and community members interested in the process are expected to be able to weigh in as the committee progresses through its review over the coming months.

item.content:encoded:
Bay Minette, AL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Bay Minette Police say a 17-year-old boy shot an 18-year-old man Thursday afternoon near Newport Parkway. The victim was taken to a Mobile hospital with non-life-threatening injuries to his upper leg.


A school bus with children on board happened to be driving through the area during the shooting, though no kids were hurt.


Police are also charging a fifteen-year-old with possessing a stolen gun after determining he wasn't connected to the shooting itself. A twenty-three-year-old man detained alongside the teen shooter is still being questioned.

item.content:encoded: Escambia County, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County and Commissioner Steve Stroberger are hosting a community open house on the Local Option Sales Tax next Tuesday at the Bellview Library. The free event starts at five and gives residents a chance to see fire trucks and ambulances purchased through L-O-S-T, along with information on its upcoming renewal. The Bellview Library itself was funded through the same tax, opening in 2022 as District One's first public library.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos bounced back Thursday night with a 7-2 victory over the Biloxi Shuckers, keeping their season moving in the right direction.

Pitcher Luis Moreno delivered a strong start for Pensacola, while the offense got contributions from Aiva Arquette and Max Williams, both of whom went deep. The back-to-back homers powered what became a comfortable margin of victory.

Thursday's win marked the first time in this series the Blue Wahoos struck first on the scoreboard, a sign of early momentum that could carry into upcoming matchups against the Shuckers.

item.title: North Escambia Volunteers Launch Pedestrian Safety Audits
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A team of volunteers fanned out Thursday evening across North Escambia to evaluate the condition of crosswalks, sidewalks, and pedestrian accessibility as part of an ongoing AARP Community Challenge grant project. The so-called "walk audits" will examine several high-traffic areas over the coming weeks, including routes along East Hecker Road, the…
item.content:encoded:
A team of volunteers fanned out Thursday evening across North Escambia to evaluate the condition of crosswalks, sidewalks, and pedestrian accessibility as part of an ongoing AARP Community Challenge grant project. The so-called "walk audits" will examine several high-traffic areas over the coming weeks, including routes along East Hecker Road, the area around a Dollar General location on East Hecker Road, and nearby Food Giant.

The audits are designed to identify safety concerns and accessibility issues that affect how easily residents can walk through their community. By documenting conditions on the ground, volunteers hope to pinpoint specific improvements that could make pedestrian travel safer and more convenient in North Escambia's busiest commercial zones.

The AARP-backed initiative reflects growing recognition that walkability and pedestrian safety are critical quality-of-life issues, particularly for older adults and people with mobility challenges. Results from the audits are expected to inform future infrastructure decisions in the area.

item.title: Local Navy Officer Recalls Being Yards Away From Pentagon Attack
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A retired Pensacola Navy public affairs officer has shared his firsthand account of being inside the Pentagon during the September 11, 2001 terrorist attack, according to reporting from North Escambia. Steve Vanderwerff, who worked for Naval Education and Training Command based in Pensacola, was in his office at the Pentagon that morning when…
item.content:encoded:
A retired Pensacola Navy public affairs officer has shared his firsthand account of being inside the Pentagon during the September 11, 2001 terrorist attack, according to reporting from North Escambia.

Steve Vanderwerff, who worked for Naval Education and Training Command based in Pensacola, was in his office at the Pentagon that morning when American Airlines Flight 77 struck the building. His workspace was less than 100 yards around the corner from where the plane impacted the structure.

Vanderwerff's experience places him among the thousands of Pentagon employees and military personnel who witnessed the immediate aftermath of one of the deadliest terrorist attacks on American soil. The crash killed 184 people inside the building and on the aircraft.

Now retired, Vanderwerff has chosen to document his experience from that day, offering a personal perspective on how the attack unfolded for those working inside the Pentagon's corridors when it happened.

item.title: Florida Executes Daniel Conahan for 1996 Charlotte County Murder
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida carried out the execution of Daniel Owen Conahan Jr. on Thursday evening at Florida State Prison, ending a nearly three-decade legal process that began with a brutal killing in Charlotte County. Conahan, 72, was pronounced dead at 6:12 p.m. following a lethal injection, according to the state Division of Corrections. Conahan was convicted…
item.content:encoded:
Florida carried out the execution of Daniel Owen Conahan Jr. on Thursday evening at Florida State Prison, ending a nearly three-decade legal process that began with a brutal killing in Charlotte County. Conahan, 72, was pronounced dead at 6:12 p.m. following a lethal injection, according to the state Division of Corrections.

Conahan was convicted in the 1996 strangulation death of Richard Allen Montgomery, a 21-year-old whose case had haunted law enforcement for decades. The execution marked one of Florida's ongoing capital punishment cases, reflecting the lengthy appeals process that typically follows death sentences in the state.

The case centered on Charlotte County, located south of the Tampa Bay area, and the conviction ultimately led to Conahan's death sentence. While Florida has reduced its execution pace in recent years, Thursday's execution represented the state's continued use of capital punishment for cases involving violent crimes.

item.title: 25 Years Later: Pensacola Remembers September 11
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: As we mark a quarter-century since the September 11 attacks, the Pensacola community is reflecting on where they were that morning and how the tragedy shaped the decades that followed. September 11, 2001, began like any other day for most Americans, but by mid-morning, four coordinated terrorist attacks had changed the nation forever. In the…
item.content:encoded:
As we mark a quarter-century since the September 11 attacks, the Pensacola community is reflecting on where they were that morning and how the tragedy shaped the decades that followed.

September 11, 2001, began like any other day for most Americans, but by mid-morning, four coordinated terrorist attacks had changed the nation forever. In the Pensacola area, thousands of residents have carried those memories for 25 years—the shock, the uncertainty, and the resilience that followed.

Local outlets are encouraging people to share their personal stories from that day. Whether you were at work, at home, or at one of our local military installations, these individual accounts help preserve the collective memory of how September 11 affected Northwest Florida. The stories matter because they remind us of where we've been and how far we've come.

For many in the Pensacola region, the significance of that day remains profound. The community continues to honor those lost and remember the first responders who answered the call. As we reflect on these 25 years, sharing where you were that September morning keeps the memory alive for future generations.

item.title: 9/11 Memorial Stands as Quiet Tribute to Nearly 3,000 Lives Lost
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: As Americans continue to process the weight of September 11, 2001, the 9/11 Memorial in lower Manhattan remains a solemn space dedicated to remembrance. Located at the site where the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center fell, the memorial honors nearly 3,000 lives lost in the terrorist attacks that morning—an event whose images remain etched in…
item.content:encoded:
As Americans continue to process the weight of September 11, 2001, the 9/11 Memorial in lower Manhattan remains a solemn space dedicated to remembrance. Located at the site where the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center fell, the memorial honors nearly 3,000 lives lost in the terrorist attacks that morning—an event whose images remain etched in the nation's collective memory.

The memorial site has become a destination for those seeking to pay respects and understand the historical significance of that day. Visitors can explore the grounds and reflect on the impact of the attacks, which reshaped American security, foreign policy, and national consciousness.

For those in the Pensacola area looking to observe the anniversary or learn more about the events of 9/11, the memorial's photo gallery and documentation offer a chance to remember those who were lost and the resilience that followed.
